verdict.rationale: Crossplane documents encapsulating permissions and guardrails behind a custom API layer that AI agents can self-service through, and extends Kubernetes RBAC to everything it orchestrates. This gives agents a scoped, least-privilege surface. There is no evidence of a plan or preview step for agent changes, or of a review or approval gate that blocks unapproved applies; the only dry-run cited is for the Helm install. missing for 10: documented plan/diff of agent-proposed changes, review/approval gates before apply, concrete least-privilege credential scoping guidance for agents, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, I can let an agent plan and apply with least-privilege credentials and review gates so it cannot make unapproved changes

citations.quote: Encapsulate policies, permissions, and other guardrails behind a custom API layer to enable consumers, whether human users, automated workflows, or AI agents, to self-service
Expose declarative APIs that humans, automation, and AI systems can safely act on
extending its battle hardened reliability and security features like Role Based Access Control (RBAC) to orchestrate everything
